description: An introduction to motion in a straight line, covering distance and displacement, speed and velocity, acceleration, scalar and vector quantities, and interpreting distance-time and velocity-time graphs.

mcq.questionText: The distance moved by a body in a stated direction is called:
mcq.explanation: Distance with direction is displacement. Exam Tip: Distance = how far (no direction); displacement = how far in a given direction.

mcq.questionText: The distance travelled by a body per unit time is called:
mcq.explanation: Distance / time is speed. Exam Tip: Speed = distance / time. SI unit metres per second (m/s).

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of speed is:
mcq.explanation: Speed = distance (m) / time (s) = m/s. Exam Tip: m/s = speed; m/s2 = acceleration.

mcq.questionText: A car travels 100 metres in 20 seconds. Its speed is:
mcq.explanation: Speed = 100 / 20 = 5 m/s. Exam Tip: Divide distance BY time. A multiplies instead.

mcq.questionText: Speed in a stated direction is called:
mcq.explanation: Speed with direction is velocity. Exam Tip: Speed = size only; velocity = size AND direction (a vector).

mcq.questionText: The rate of change of velocity with time is called:
mcq.explanation: How fast velocity changes is acceleration. Exam Tip: Acceleration = change in velocity / time. SI unit m/s2.

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of acceleration is:
mcq.explanation: Acceleration = (m/s) / s = m/s2. Exam Tip: The squared second marks acceleration.

mcq.questionText: A body moving with constant (uniform) velocity has an acceleration of:
mcq.explanation: Uniform velocity means no change in velocity, so no acceleration. Exam Tip: Constant velocity means zero acceleration.

mcq.questionText: A car increases its velocity from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 4 seconds. Its acceleration is:
mcq.explanation: a = (30 - 10) / 4 = 20 / 4 = 5 m/s2. Exam Tip: Subtract the velocities FIRST, then divide by time.

mcq.questionText: When a body slows down, it has:
mcq.explanation: A decrease in velocity is negative acceleration (deceleration). Exam Tip: Speeding up gives positive; slowing down gives negative (deceleration).

mcq.questionText: On a distance-time graph, a straight horizontal line means the body is:
mcq.explanation: A horizontal line means distance is not changing, so the body is at rest. Exam Tip: Distance-time: horizontal = at rest; sloping straight = constant speed; curve = changing speed.

mcq.questionText: On a distance-time graph, the speed of the body is given by the:
mcq.explanation: Speed = distance / time = rise / run = slope (gradient). Exam Tip: Distance-time graph: gradient = speed. Steeper line = higher speed.

mcq.questionText: A bus travels 60 km in 2 hours. Its average speed is:
mcq.explanation: Average speed = 60 / 2 = 30 km/h. Exam Tip: Average speed uses TOTAL distance / TOTAL time; keep units consistent.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a vector quantity (has both size and direction)?
mcq.explanation: Velocity is speed in a stated direction - a vector. Exam Tip: Vectors: displacement, velocity, acceleration, force. Scalars: distance, speed, time, mass.

mcq.questionText: A body starts from rest. Its initial velocity is:
mcq.explanation: Starts from rest means not moving, so zero velocity. Exam Tip: From rest always means initial velocity u = 0.

fib.questionText: The length of the path travelled by a body, without regard to direction, is called ____.
fib.explanation: The total path length ignoring direction is distance, a scalar. Exam Tip: Distance is a scalar; displacement is the vector version.

fib.questionText: Speed is calculated using the formula speed = distance / ____.
fib.explanation: Speed is distance divided by the time taken. Exam Tip: speed = distance / time.

fib.questionText: Speed in a stated direction is called ____.
fib.explanation: Adding a direction to speed makes it velocity. Exam Tip: Velocity is a vector; speed is a scalar.

fib.questionText: The SI unit of acceleration is ____.
fib.explanation: Acceleration is change of velocity (m/s) per second, giving m/s2. Exam Tip: Acceleration always carries m/s2.

fib.questionText: A body moving with uniform velocity has zero ____.
fib.explanation: Uniform velocity means velocity does not change, so acceleration is zero. Exam Tip: Constant velocity means acceleration = 0.

fib.questionText: The gradient (slope) of a distance-time graph gives the ____ of the body.
fib.explanation: The gradient is rise/run = distance/time = speed. Exam Tip: Distance-time gradient = speed; velocity-time gradient = acceleration.

fib.questionText: The formula for acceleration is a = (v - u) / ____, where v is final velocity and u is initial velocity.
fib.explanation: Acceleration is the change in velocity divided by the time taken. Exam Tip: a = (v - u)/t.

fib.questionText: A quantity that has only size (magnitude) but no direction is called a ____ quantity.
fib.explanation: A quantity with magnitude only and no direction is a scalar. Exam Tip: Scalars: distance, speed, mass, time.

fib.questionText: A car covering equal distances in equal intervals of time is said to be moving with ____ speed.
fib.explanation: Equal distances in equal times means the speed does not change, so it is uniform. Exam Tip: Uniform speed shows as a straight sloping line on a distance-time graph.

fib.questionText: On a velocity-time graph, the gradient (slope) represents the ____.
fib.explanation: The gradient is change in velocity divided by time, which is acceleration. Exam Tip: Velocity-time graph: gradient = acceleration; area under = distance.

tf.questionText: Distance is a scalar quantity while displacement is a vector quantity.
tf.explanation: Distance has size only while displacement has size and direction. Exam Tip: The classic scalar-vector example.

tf.questionText: Speed is calculated by multiplying distance by time.
tf.explanation: Speed is distance divided by time, not multiplied. Exam Tip: speed = distance / time (division).

tf.questionText: Velocity is speed in a stated direction.
tf.explanation: Velocity adds a direction to speed, making it a vector. Exam Tip: Speed = scalar; velocity = vector.

tf.questionText: A body moving with constant velocity is accelerating.
tf.explanation: Constant velocity means no change in velocity, so acceleration is zero. Exam Tip: Constant velocity means zero acceleration.

tf.questionText: The SI unit of acceleration is m/s2.
tf.explanation: Acceleration is measured in metres per second squared. Exam Tip: m/s2 identifies acceleration; m/s identifies speed/velocity.

tf.questionText: On a distance-time graph, a horizontal line means the body is moving fastest.
tf.explanation: A horizontal line means distance is not changing, so the body is at rest. Exam Tip: Horizontal line = at rest.

tf.questionText: Deceleration means the velocity of a body is decreasing.
tf.explanation: Deceleration is negative acceleration, a decrease in velocity. Exam Tip: Deceleration = slowing down = negative acceleration.
Time has magnitude only and no direction, so it is a scalar. Exam Tip: Time, distance, speed and mass are scalars.

tf.questionText: The gradient of a distance-time graph gives the speed of the body.
tf.explanation: The gradient equals distance divided by time, which is speed. Exam Tip: Steeper line = greater speed.

tf.questionText: A body that starts from rest has an initial velocity greater than zero.
tf.explanation: Starting from rest means the initial velocity is zero. Exam Tip: From rest means u = 0.

summary.correctAnswer: The length of the path travelled by a body, without regard to direction.
summary.explanation: Distance is a scalar quantity measured in metres. Exam Tip: Distance tells how far, with no direction.

summary.correctAnswer: The distance moved by a body in a stated direction.
summary.explanation: Displacement is a vector quantity measured in metres. Exam Tip: Displacement is distance plus direction.

summary.correctAnswer: The distance travelled per unit time, given by speed = distance / time.
summary.explanation: Speed is a scalar measured in m/s. Exam Tip: Divide distance by time to get speed.

summary.correctAnswer: The speed of a body in a stated direction, that is the rate of change of displacement.
summary.explanation: Velocity is a vector measured in m/s. Exam Tip: Velocity has both size and direction.

summary.correctAnswer: The rate of change of velocity with time, given by a = (v - u) / t.
summary.explanation: Acceleration is a vector measured in m/s2. Exam Tip: Subtract u from v first, then divide by time.

summary.correctAnswer: A scalar has size only, while a vector has both size and direction.
summary.explanation: Distance, speed, time and mass are scalars; displacement, velocity and force are vectors. Exam Tip: Ask whether direction matters to decide.

summary.correctAnswer: Motion in which a body covers equal distances in equal intervals of time in a fixed direction, so acceleration is zero.
summary.explanation: Uniform velocity gives a straight sloping line on a distance-time graph. Exam Tip: Uniform velocity means zero acceleration.

summary.correctAnswer: The gradient (slope) of a distance-time graph gives the speed of the body.
summary.explanation: A steeper line means a higher speed; a horizontal line means at rest. Exam Tip: Distance-time gradient = speed.

summary.correctAnswer: The gradient (slope) of a velocity-time graph gives the acceleration of the body.
summary.explanation: The area under a velocity-time graph gives the distance travelled. Exam Tip: Velocity-time gradient = acceleration.

summary.correctAnswer: The total distance travelled divided by the total time taken for the whole journey.
summary.explanation: Average speed uses totals, including any resting time. Exam Tip: Use TOTAL distance / TOTAL time.

hoq.questionText: A cyclist travels 150 m east in 30 s, rests for 10 s, then travels 90 m east in 20 s. Find the average speed for the WHOLE journey.
hoq.explanation: Total distance = 150 + 90 = 240 m. Total time = 30 + 10 + 20 = 60 s. Average speed = 240 / 60 = 4 m/s. Exam Tip: Average speed uses TOTAL distance and TOTAL time - include the rest time. Forgetting the 10 s gives 4.8 m/s (the trap).

hoq.questionText: A car accelerates uniformly from rest and reaches 24 m/s in 8 s. Find its acceleration, then how far it travels using distance = average velocity x time.
hoq.explanation: a = (24 - 0) / 8 = 3 m/s2. Average velocity = (0 + 24)/2 = 12 m/s. Distance = 12 x 8 = 96 m. Exam Tip: From rest means u = 0. Average velocity is (u + v)/2, not the final velocity.

hoq.questionText: A runner's position every 2 s: 0 s to 0 m, 2 s to 10 m, 4 s to 20 m, 6 s to 30 m, 8 s to 40 m. Describe the motion and calculate the speed.

options.text: The runner speeds up; speed = 40 m/s
The runner moves at constant speed; speed = 5 m/s
The runner is at rest; speed = 0 m/s
The runner slows down; speed = 2 m/s

hoq.explanation: Each 2 s interval covers 10 m (equal distances in equal times) = constant speed. Speed = 10 / 2 = 5 m/s. Exam Tip: Equal distances in equal time = uniform speed. Compute speed from any matching interval.
